clue.text: Musical soldiers in line

parts.note: GI is the usual crossword word for an American soldier
the plural gives a second GI, set beside the first

explanation.surface: Troops standing in a row, perhaps on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' is plural, so it supplies two GIs; 'in line' tells you to set them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is a Lerner and Loewe stage and film show, an example of the genre.

clue.text: First-rate battle I'd engaged in, on this date

parts.note: first-rate means good

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so one piece sits inside the battle word

parts.note: a fray is a fight or battle
I'd contracts I had or I would, giving the letters ID

explanation.surface: A diary entry recording that a fine fight took place on this day.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only 'this date'; 'on' is a link, letting the clue read as a dated battle report.
explanation.definitionFit: The holiday before Easter is a fixed day in the Christian calendar, so it is a date.

clue.text: Rising, in order to have caught for example, a lizard

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the whole run of letters reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: in order means all right, OK
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A muddled sentence about something climbing in order to catch something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the whole string OKCEG around, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Geckos are small wall-climbing reptiles, a kind of lizard.

clue.text: Birds separate, perching on roof-tops

indicators.note: perching on places one piece ahead of the other, sitting at the front

parts.note: to separate is to part
the ridges are the top lines of roofs

explanation.surface: Birds separate from the flock and settle on the tops of roofs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birds' and 'perching' make the surface feel natural, but 'separate' is a verb supplying PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Partridges are game birds of the pheasant family.

clue.text: Examining body finding gold outperforms yen

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
to outperform is to top
Y abbreviates yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Financial news: gold is doing better than the Japanese currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The money words make it read like market news; 'finding' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem is the examination of a dead body.

clue.text: Containers for dried leaves

parts.note: the dried leaves sound like a herbarium or autumn foliage but are tea, packed in small porous sachets

explanation.surface: A description of storage for pressed or fallen leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is dried leaves, and these small paper pouches hold a single portion for brewing.

clue.text: Found an entrance, apparently, to the bar

parts.note: an entrance is a way in, so IN
found means got, as in got in

explanation.surface: Someone finally found the way into the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found an entrance' is 'got in'; 'apparently' says to read the answer as those two words in the other order.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, such as gold.

clue.text: In glass I'd shattered, playing, while sliding up and down the passages

definitions.text: sliding up and down the passages
definitions.note: a description of musical slides through runs of notes, standing for the plural noun

indicators.note: glass that is shattered breaks into pieces, so these letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A musician's glass is smashed mid-performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges INGLASSID; 'playing, while' is link material setting the musical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a glissando is a rapid slide over a run of notes, and the plural follows the Italian form.

clue.text: It's cut down in a twisted position

definitions.meaning: the past tense of slay, killed
a turned or skewed position, as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: Slay's past form means killed, and the noun names a sideways swing or twisted lie of something.

clue.text: Fellows affirm it covers their bodies

parts.note: fellows are men
to affirm is to swear, as on oath

explanation.surface: Men declare something about what they wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'Fellows', so the whole clue reads as one thought.
explanation.definitionFit: The clothing sold for males is what clothes them.

clue.text: Fiddling accounts for a few of these pit workers

definitions.text: Fiddling accounts for a few of these pit workers

parts.words: Fiddling accounts for a few of these pit workers
parts.note: fiddling and accounts suggest fraud, and pit workers suggest coal miners, but the fiddling is violin playing and the pit is the theatre's music area

explanation.surface: Fraudulent bookkeeping involves a handful of miners.
explanation.definitionFit: The musicians in a theatre pit form this ensemble, and violinists make up part of it.

clue.text: Keep on complaining about the pain

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means grumble, and the noun, usually plural, is a spasm in the bowels.

clue.text: On first sighting animal turns tail, then runs

indicators.note: On means coming next to, so the picked letter goes after the turned animal
turns tail means flees, here telling you to turn the animal word around

parts.note: the wolf is the animal

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word sighting

explanation.surface: An animal, on first being spotted, turns and runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns tail' reverses WOLF to FLOW; 'On first sighting' adds the S of 'sighting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid that flows moves along steadily, as a river runs.

clue.text: Contrive by some means to scrape it off

indicators.note: off means wrong or bad, so these letters go into another order

explanation.surface: Advice to get something off a surface by scraping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SCRAPEIT; 'by some means to' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense to practise is to scheme or plot, as in practising deceit.

clue.text: Reason for ambassador turning up inside with unspecified number of dogs

indicators.note: inside places the turned piece within the reason word

parts.note: grounds are reasons

indicators.note: with here means holding, so the number goes inside the title
in a down clue turning up reverses the letters to read from the bottom

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title
Y is an algebra letter for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: The excuse for an envoy arriving with a pack of dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, the formal title of an ambassador; 'with' here means holding, 'turning up' reverses as this is a down clue, and 'inside' places the result within the reason word.
explanation.definitionFit: These slim racing hounds are a breed of dog.

clue.text: Yet, foolishly pursuing warrior band is sacrilege

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the rearranged letters follow the band

parts.note: an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors

indicators.note: acting foolishly means acting in a muddled way, so this word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Chasing a group of warriors is, oddly, an offence against the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: An impi is a Zulu regiment, a South African term crosswords use often; 'is' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean irreverence towards what is holy.

clue.text: Filter may be awkward to replace

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so these letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A filter can be fiddly to swap for a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: To percolate is to pass slowly through a porous medium, as coffee does.

clue.text: Top bowler

definitions.meaning: a cricket bowler who spins the ball

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a toy that whirls and a cricketer who imparts spin; cricket is a bat-and-ball game popular in Britain.

clue.text: I yell, they say, then dessert will appear

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are heard spoken, not written

parts.note: I yell means I scream

explanation.surface: A cry of delight that announces pudding is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: This frozen sweet is served as a pudding after the main course.

clue.text: Coming from a mess, they may be scrambled

definitions.text: Coming from a mess, they may be scrambled

parts.words: Coming from a mess, they may be scrambled
parts.note: a mess and scrambled suggest a kitchen and eggs, but the mess is an air force dining room and scrambling is an urgent take-off

explanation.surface: Something from a messy kitchen, perhaps scrambled eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying personnel eat in an officers' mess and are ordered into the air in a hurry.

clue.text: Manx cat can initially get fish

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the whip word loses its last letter

parts.note: cat is short for cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip
a can is a tin

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word get

explanation.surface: A tailless cat can at first get hold of a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' (the tailless breed) docks WHIP to WHI; 'initially' takes G from 'get'.
explanation.definitionFit: This small sea creature is a member of the cod family.

clue.text: Soul's wit

parts.note: a nod to Polonius in Hamlet, who says that this quality is the soul of wit

explanation.surface: A person's spirit and humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare calls shortness of expression the soul of wit, so the phrase points to it.

clue.text: Sometimes made to hold one's breath

definitions.text: Sometimes made to hold one's breath

parts.words: Sometimes made to hold one's breath
parts.note: holding one's breath suggests suspense or diving, but here the breath is blown into a rubber toy

explanation.surface: Someone is made to hold their breath, perhaps by a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A party inflatable is filled with exhaled air and keeps it in.

clue.text: Result of minor excavation — strange hole's appearance in factory

indicators.note: appearance in means turning up within, so the rearranged letters go inside the factory word

parts.note: a mill is a factory

indicators.note: strange means odd, so these letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A small dig leaves an odd hole in a factory floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hole's' carries a possessive that adds no letter; the definition is a playful description of a mound thrown up by a burrowing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small burrowing animal leaves a mound of earth when it tunnels, a little dig.

clue.text: Sees a manipulation provides relief

indicators.note: manipulation means handling and moving, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sees that a massage gives relief.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve pain or tension is to lessen it.

clue.text: Boy calls for turnover, with duck

parts.note: a turnover is a turning over, a roll
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A lad orders a pastry together with some duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calls for' is link; 'turnover' and 'duck' look like menu items.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollo is a boy's name, borne by the Viking founder of Normandy.

clue.text: Not standing for dishonesty

explanation.definitionFit: The word means stretched out horizontally and also deceiving with falsehoods.

clue.text: Stay of sentence

parts.note: a stay of sentence suggests a legal delay in punishment, but the sentence here is grammatical, and the halt is its closing dot

explanation.surface: A judge postpones a convict's punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop halts a written sentence, and the word also means stay, as in halt.

clue.text: Transport bringing back spruce

indicators.note: bringing back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: spruce means neat, smart

explanation.surface: A vehicle brings a fir tree back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Street railcars are a means of public conveyance.

clue.text: Diverting into Laos, I find solitude

indicators.note: diverting means turning aside, so these letters are sent into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller rerouted into Laos discovers peace and quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone and apart from others is a near synonym of being cut off.

clue.text: His job to put the squeeze on a chap?

definitions.text: His job to put the squeeze on a chap?

parts.words: His job to put the squeeze on a chap?
parts.note: putting the squeeze on suggests extortion, but the squeezing is pressing, done by a publicity man for the newspapers

explanation.surface: A heavy whose task is leaning on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A publicist's work is getting a client into the newspapers, the media.

clue.text: Silver-headed, like some rulers

indicators.note: headed means coming at the head, so the silver symbol goes in front

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
as means like

explanation.surface: Some monarchs have white hair.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is an Ottoman title for a commander or chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Agas were Ottoman military commanders and officials, figures of authority.
